hook.text: A test is 99% accurate. You test positive. Most people think there's a 99% chance you're sick. Wrong.

buildup.text: If the disease affects 1 in 10,000 people, most positives are false. The base rate changes everything.

discovery.text: Base rate neglect means ignoring how common something is and focusing only on the specific evidence.

twist.text: Bayes' theorem fixes this by combining the test result with the prior probability. Few people use it intuitively.

climax.text: In courts, juries convict on vivid evidence while ignoring that the crime type is extremely rare.

punchline.text: How common it is matters more than how well it fits.

quiz.question: What is base rate neglect?
options: Ignoring how common something is when judging probability

details.summary: People routinely ignore base rate statistics in favor of specific case information. When told that 1 percent of a population has a disease and a test is 90 percent accurate, most people drastically overestimate the probability of actually having the disease given a positive test result.
details.whyItMatters: Base rate neglect causes misinterpretation of medical tests, criminal profiling, and risk assessments. It makes rare events seem common when a specific case matches a vivid description.
takeaways: Specific case details override statistical base rates in judgment
People overestimate probabilities after a positive test or match
Bayesian reasoning corrects base rate neglect

faq.question: Why is base rate neglect a problem in medical testing?
faq.answer: If a disease affects 1 in 1,000 people and a test has a 5 percent false positive rate, a positive result still means only about a 2 percent chance of having the disease. Most positives are false positives. Without understanding base rates, patients and doctors overreact to positive results.

faq.question: How can Bayesian reasoning help?
faq.answer: Bayesian reasoning combines the base rate of an event with new evidence to calculate the updated probability. It forces you to start with how common something is before adjusting based on specific information. This approach systematically corrects the intuitive neglect of base rates.
